Claude; synthesise research with Claude and
Designing how Torob’s AI answers product questions — co-created with the Data team and connected to Nearby.
Search answers “which product is this?”, but many users ask “which one should I buy?”. In
research, 54% wanted consultation before buying — the guidance a good seller gives in
store. They had no way to get it online.
Led the conversation and answer design. Worked closely with the Data team to shape the
answer algorithm: intent detection, category rules, ranking and badge logic, follow-up
The conversation stays anchored to the product the user came from.
Scannable scenarios (light, medium, heavy use) instead of long paragraphs.
Best pick per scenario, with price and badges like Good value or Top-rated.
Every answer ends with deeper questions to keep the conversation going.
We chose short, title-style answers and moved the detail into follow-up questions — easier to
scan on mobile, and a natural reason to keep the conversation going.
Why an AI assistant: how users really search
Sample of 57K+ Torob search queries, tagged by query type — with the Data team
Half of searches named an exact product, which classic search handles well. But 37% described a need instead of a product (a specific
feature or use case, like “black sports trousers” or “lamp for a gaming room”), and 8% were too unclear to classify. Keyword search
struggles with these, so they became the core use case for the AI Shopping Assistant: understand the need, recommend options and
One assistant, three ways of answering
Using the search-intent framework from Iteration 2, the assistant first detects what the user is trying to do, then picks the answer format.

phone?” — it shows the Nearby seller component with phone number,
address and directions, turning an AI answer into a store visit.
